description: Generate a slide-deck-quality 2×2 matrix, the classic consulting quadrant slide: two labelled axes (name plus low and high ends, rotated on the left) and four quadrants tinted in one accent colour. Two modes: "plot" places items as dots at x and y on 0–10 scales (or bubbles sized by `size`), with every label placed automatically so none overlap and quadrant names faint in the corners; "list" gives each quadrant a bold name and up to 6 bullets. Choose it to prioritise or position things on two dimensions: tasks, initiatives, features, products, brands, stakeholders or risks. Pick the preset that matches the request and let it supply the standard axes, quadrant names and mode: impactEffort for impact vs effort, quick wins or an action priority matrix; eisenhower for urgent vs important or a to-do list; bcg for a growth-share or product portfolio matrix (give revenue as size); ansoff for growth strategy (products × markets); powerInterest for a stakeholder map; perceptual for a perceptual or competitive positioning map (rename the axes to the user's attributes); riskLikelihood for a likelihood vs impact risk grid; none for any other 2×2 (name the axes and quadrants yourself; an omitted preset means none). Quadrants are keyed by position: topLeft, topRight, bottomLeft, bottomRight; with normal axes topRight is high x, high y. Use a Harvey ball matrix to score options against several criteria, create_five_forces for one industry's competitive forces, and create_swot for strengths, weaknesses, opportunities and threats. Infer realistic positions from context rather than asking. Limits: 30 items, names up to 40 characters (1–4 words read best), 6 bullets per quadrant. Infer missing details rather than asking; the user can adjust the chart in the builder through the Edit link. ALWAYS give the user the image link: inline chat images usually cannot be saved, but the link renders the exact chart on demand and can be pasted into a slide or Markdown.

bullets.description: List mode: 0–6 short bullets under the name, e.g. ["Board deck due Friday", "Server outage follow-up"]. Each wraps to at most 3 lines.

color.description: Optional hex colour for this quadrant's tint (and its plot dots), e.g. "#10b981". Default: the accent (first palette colour).

name.description: Quadrant name, e.g. "Quick wins". Bold at the top of the quadrant in list mode, faint in its outer corner in plot mode. Omit to use the preset's name; "" hides it.

inputSchema.description: A 2×2 matrix: two axes and four labelled quadrants. In list mode each quadrant holds a name and bullets (Eisenhower, Ansoff); in plot mode items are dots or bubbles placed by x and y (impact–effort, BCG, power–interest, perceptual maps). A preset fills in standard axis labels, quadrant names and the mode.

credit.description: Shows a small "twominutetoolkit.com" credit under the chart, inside the card. Set false to leave it off (for example when the user asks for no branding).

items.description: Plot mode only (kept but not drawn in list mode): 0–30 items, each a dot at its x and y on 0–10 scales, with its name beside it, e.g. { "name": "Self-serve onboarding", "x": 2.5, "y": 8 }. Labels are placed automatically so they never overlap. Give `size` to draw bubbles.

color.description: Optional hex colour for this dot, e.g. "#ef4444" to flag one item. Default: its quadrant's colour, which is the accent unless that quadrant has its own.

name.description: Label shown beside the dot at 13px, e.g. "SSO for enterprise". Keep it to 1–4 words; long names wrap to two lines.

size.description: Optional bubble size, any positive number such as revenue (e.g. 420 for $420m). Bubble AREA is proportional to size, relative to the largest; items without a size stay small dots. Omit on every item for plain dots.

x.description: Position along the horizontal axis, 0 (low) to 10 (high); 5 is the midline. Default 5.

y.description: Position along the vertical axis, 0 (low) to 10 (high); 5 is the midline. Default 5.

mode.description: "list": four tinted quadrants, each with its name and bullets. "plot": items drawn as dots or bubbles at their x and y, with quadrant names faint in the corners. Omit to use the preset's mode (list for eisenhower and ansoff, plot for the rest).

palette.description: Hex colours. The whole matrix uses the FIRST palette colour as its one accent, tinted in four strengths across the quadrants, so a brand colour as the first entry recolours the chart. Default: indigo, sky, emerald, amber, red, gray.

preset.description: Set it: the standard matrix to start from, or "none" (the default when omitted). Its axis labels, quadrant names and mode fill in anything the payload leaves out (your own values always win). eisenhower: urgency (urgent on the LEFT) × importance; Do first, Schedule, Delegate, Eliminate; list. impactEffort: effort × impact; Quick wins (top left), Major projects, Fill-ins, Thankless tasks; plot. bcg: relative market share (high on the LEFT) × market growth; Stars, Question marks, Cash cows, Dogs; plot. ansoff: products (existing, new) across × markets (existing at the TOP, new below); Market penetration, Product development, Market development, Diversification; list. powerInterest: interest × power; Keep satisfied, Manage closely, Monitor, Keep informed; plot. perceptual: price × quality; High value, Premium, Economy, Overpriced; plot. riskLikelihood: likelihood × impact; Plan contingency, Act now, Accept, Monitor; plot. none: plain Low/High axes and no quadrant names, plot (name the axes and quadrants yourself).

quadrants.description: The four quadrants by POSITION on the slide (after any axis reversal): topLeft, topRight, bottomLeft, bottomRight. With both axes in their normal direction, topRight is high x and high y, bottomLeft low x and low y. Each is { "name", "bullets", "color" }, all optional; a missing name comes from the preset. E.g. { "topLeft": { "name": "Quick wins", "bullets": ["Fix checkout bug"] } }.

bottomLeft.description: Bottom-left quadrant: low x and low y when the axes run normally (impactEffort: Fill-ins; bcg: Cash cows).

bottomRight.description: Bottom-right quadrant: high x and low y when the axes run normally (impactEffort: Thankless tasks; bcg: Dogs).

topLeft.description: Top-left quadrant: low x and high y when the axes run normally (impactEffort: Quick wins; eisenhower: Do first; bcg: Stars).

topRight.description: Top-right quadrant: high x and high y when the axes run normally (impactEffort: Major projects; powerInterest: Manage closely).

showGrid.description: Plot mode: light gridlines at every whole unit (1–9) behind the items. Default false (the midlines only).

title.description: Heading shown top-left of the chart at 22px bold. Every chart has one title row; an empty string hides it.

width.description: Chart width in pixels (640–2400, default 1280, which suits a 16:9 slide). PNG output renders at 2x. Height follows from the width (plot mode) or the bullets (list mode).

xAxis.description: The horizontal axis along the bottom, e.g. { "label": "Effort", "low": "Low", "high": "High" }. Each field you omit comes from the preset; an empty string hides that text.

high.description: Text at the high end, e.g. "High", "New" or "Urgent".

label.description: Axis name, centred under the matrix in bold, e.g. "Effort" or "Relative market share".

low.description: Text at the low end, e.g. "Low", "Existing" or "Not urgent".

reverse.description: true puts the HIGH end on the left (BCG share, Eisenhower urgency). Item x values still mean low (0) to high (10). Default: the preset's direction, else false (high on the right).

yAxis.description: The vertical axis up the left side, with rotated texts, e.g. { "label": "Impact", "low": "Low", "high": "High" }. Each field you omit comes from the preset; an empty string hides that text.

high.description: Text at the high end, e.g. "High" or "Important".

label.description: Axis name, centred beside the matrix in bold, e.g. "Impact" or "Market growth".

low.description: Text at the low end, e.g. "Low" or "Not important".

reverse.description: true puts the HIGH end at the bottom (Ansoff: existing markets on top). Item y values still mean low (0) to high (10). Default: the preset's direction, else false (high at the top).
